purpose: Resolve Trifolium feeding evidence by tortoise taxon and plant identification level without converting wild observations into captive feeding prescriptions.

canonical_interpretation.exact_ibera_support: Direct wild Testudo graeca ibera evidence exists for Trifolium at genus level in Dobrogea, Romania (Iftime & Iftime 2012).
canonical_interpretation.species_resolution_limit: The exact-Ibera record does not establish Trifolium repens, T. campestre, or another named Trifolium species as the consumed taxon.
canonical_interpretation.related_testudo_species_records: Exact species records include Trifolium campestre in wild Testudo hermanni and Trifolium repens in a semi-natural T. h. boettgeri husbandry context.
canonical_interpretation.bulgaria_boundary: Mitrevichin 2023 reported Trifolium sp., including T. campestre, for T. hermanni; the T. graeca ibera observations in that study listed other taxa and must not be relabeled as Trifolium evidence for Ibera.
canonical_interpretation.verdict_rule: These records support taxon-resolved evidence context only. They do not by themselves justify genus-wide safety, daily/unlimited feeding, staple status, captive percentages, or a stronger public feeding verdict.

records.citation: Iftime A, Iftime O. 2012. Testudo graeca ibera feeding ecology in Dobrogea, Romania. Acta Herpetologica.
records.plant_part_context: young leaves reported among preferred plant material
supports: Wild T. g. ibera directly consumed Trifolium taxon material.
Trifolium belongs in the exact-Ibera evidence layer at genus resolution.
does_not_support: Identification as Trifolium repens, Trifolium campestre, or any other exact Trifolium species.
Captive feeding frequency, percentage, daily use, unlimited use, or staple status.

records.citation: Mitrevichin E. 2023. Notes on the diet of Testudo hermanni boettgeri and T. graeca ibera in south-western Bulgaria. ZooNotes 228:1-4.
records.plant_resolution: species present for at least some observations
supports: Wild T. hermanni directly consumed Trifolium, including an exact T. campestre record.
does_not_support: A Trifolium record for the T. graeca ibera individuals in the same paper.
Genus-wide captive safety or feeding frequency.

records.citation: Del Vecchio S et al. 2011. Seasonal changes in the diet of Testudo hermanni hermanni in central Italy. Herpetologica 67(3).
supports: Trifolium leaf material occurred in wild T. h. hermanni diet samples.
does_not_support: An exact Trifolium species identity for consumed material.

records.citation: Study of Testudo hermanni diet in Garraf Natural Park, north-eastern Spain; fecal remains analysis.
supports: Exact T. campestre seed material was identified in wild T. hermanni fecal remains.
does_not_support: Leaf feeding frequency or captive diet role.

records.citation: Rouag R et al. 2008. Food choice of an Algerian population of the spur-thighed tortoise, Testudo graeca. African Journal of Herpetology 57(2).
supports: Trifolium was a commonly identified genus in this wild T. graeca population.
does_not_support: Transfer of reported fragment percentages to captive diets.
Exact species identity or exact-Ibera population evidence.

records.citation: Bielli M et al. 2015. Hematological values for adult eastern Hermann's tortoise (Testudo hermanni boettgeri) in semi-natural conditions.
records.study_type: clinical reference study with described usual husbandry diet
supports: T. repens was part of the described usual wild-plant diet for clinically examined T. h. boettgeri in semi-natural conditions.
does_not_support: A controlled safety trial of T. repens.
Exact-Ibera evidence, an optimal inclusion rate, or unlimited feeding.

guardrails: Do not rewrite the exact-Ibera Trifolium genus record as T. repens or T. campestre.
Do not transfer T. campestre records from T. hermanni to T. g. ibera as direct evidence.
Do not transfer T. repens husbandry use in T. h. boettgeri into a controlled safety claim.
Do not convert wild occurrence, preference, or fecal fragment frequency into captive diet percentages or frequency prescriptions.
Do not infer all Trifolium species are interchangeable or equally suitable.
